title: Almagris: un souls-lite oscuro en voxel pixel-art, con motor propio en Three.js
author: Protocontext
selftext:
I’ve been working on this for about three months and I finally felt like showing it.

No Unity, no Godot. I built my own engine on top of Three.js and everything runs in the browser. The first months I worked with Claude, and this last month with Astra + Opus 5.5 on the engine. I’d say AI has done about 40% of the work. The rest, especially the combat feel, the bosses, the levels and the story, I’ve been polishing by hand, through a lot of trial and error.

It’s a souls-lite, not a real Souls. If you’ve played Tunic, it’s in that direction: that Zelda/Souls mix, but darker and quite a bit crueler. There are bonfires where you heal, refill your flasks and enemies respawn. That’s where you level up (Health, Stamina, Strength, Ember) and forge your sword with steel shards. If you die, you drop your souls and get only one chance to recover them. Stamina governs everything, the roll has i-frames, the parry is timing-based and lets you riposte, and the sword can be thrown like a boomerang.

My favorite part is what happens when a boss kills you: it sends you to its underworld and you have to fight your way out to get back to the last bonfire you rested at. Every time you die down there, it sends you further back. And in Hardcore, each death snuffs out one of five candles; when they’re all out, your save is wiped.

The demo is free and runs in the browser, with Normal and Hardcore modes. Works with keyboard, Xbox controller or touch: 

[https://almagris.vercel.app/](https://almagris.vercel.app/)

It still needs work, I won’t lie, but I think you can already see where it’s going. This would be about 20% of what I have in mind.

I’d like to know what you think, both about the game and the way it’s being made. What feels off, what you’d change, and how you handle combat feel yourselves when working with AI. That’s what I’ll use to decide whether it’s worth continuing and telling the whole story :)

comments.author: Playful-Advisor-9559
comments.body: reminds me of minecraft dungeons did u make all the animations?

replies.author: Protocontext
replies.body:
Yeah, I drew a bit of inspiration from Dungeons to make the game accessible less serious than a "Souls" game. I don’t know, I just feel like this particular angle hadn’t really been explored yet!

  
For the animations, Opus created an animation system within the engine itself, which allows for testing thousands of different configurations and tweaking them by hand the "foundation" is built right inside the engine.
